title: Friendly with club operators and gangsters; Prohibition
summary: He says the so-called gangsters owned clubs that employed musicians, and discusses Prohibition drinking.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: But in Kansas City I also have always been friendly with operators. You know, like people that owned the clubs and...they used to call people gangsters and all that. Well, I always was friendly with people.

Mmmh...what is a gangster? I don't know what a gangster is, for want of a better word. I never saw any wrongdoing. I say this--I say that many of those persons that were accused of being gangsters, and all, were the ones that
had night clubs and places where musicians worked. So, if they were gangsters, they gave a lot of people work.
I guess Prohibition had something to do with that...were involved with selling liquor and it was illegal and you got........

Well, Prohibition was illegal ...well, everybody drank, so I mean, so they must have been getting the whiskey someplace. And perhaps...you know, writers create titles and pseudonyms and make references to certain things. And I know a lot of writers that wrote about Prohibition and were drunk, or they drank. And that was the purpose of going out, you know.
